'''Ingrid Christensen Kildegaard''' (died September 2, 1984 in [[Haines Falls, New York]]) was an American statistician and [[market research]]er who worked at the [[Advertising Research Foundation]] as a vice president and technical director.{{r|nyt}}

== Early life ==
Kildegaard graduated from [[Central Michigan University]] (Michigan State Teachers College) in 1936.{{r|centralight|minn}} She did her graduate studies at the [[University of Minnesota]], completing a master's degree in statistics there in 1950.{{r|nyt|minn|mincon}}

== Career ==
She joined the Advertising Research Foundation in 1956 and was promoted to director of technical services in 1965.{{r|rostworowski}} At around that time, she became involved in discussions with the [[United States Census Bureau]] over whether they should survey ownership of advanced television sets capable of color and of receiving [[UHF]] signals.{{r|census}} In 1970 she served as chair of the Subsection on Statistics in Marketing of the [[American Statistical Association]].{{r|subsection}} She retired in 1982.{{r|nyt}}

==Recognition==
In 1967, she was elected as a [[Fellow of the American Statistical Association]].{{r|fasa}} The Market Research Council added her to their Hall of Fame in 2007.{{r|hall}}
